text: iPhone port step 3: the iOS shell, built on hosted macOS CI, TestFlight

From T-352: on iOS, SystemBarIcons and DialogEdgeToEdge are no-ops and deepLinkUri returns null, so invite links need iOS routing here. Strings.kt builds ResourceEnvironment through the resources library internal constructor (suppressed INVISIBLE_MEMBER); a Compose resources upgrade may break it, StringsTest pins it.

Premise changed on 2026-11-01: the maintainer has a macOS guest (OSX-KVM, Intel, Xcode 16.2, iOS 18.3.1 simulator; see /workspace/macvm) reachable over SSH, so the shell is built, linked and run in the simulator there, not on hosted CI. The simulator is x86_64: build for iosX64 (T-373). TestFlight/CI stay with T-355. Kotlin side ready: startIosApp() and MainViewController() in shared/src/iosMain/…/ios/IosApp.kt (T-349).

Built and run on the macOS guest: ios/Tuppu.xcodeproj (scheme Tuppu, Config.xcconfig; the Compile Kotlin phase runs :shared:embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode) installs on the simulator. Found: the guest has no Metal device at all (VMware SVGA; MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice() is nil), and Compose on iOS has no software renderer (JetBrains wontfix, compose-multiplatform #3443/#4415), so the shared UI ends the process there. ContentView now shows a notice when no Metal device exists, and TuppuTests (XCTest hosted by the app) drive the platform layer through IosServices (:shared's iosMain): Keychain, and login → list → item → two syncs → account removal against the dev server on the guest (~/srv, https://localhost:8723, cert trusted via simctl keychain). All pass on the simulator. Swift sees :core's types only with export(project(":core")) on the framework, which needs the Koin BOM as an api dependency; suspend functions are callable from any Swift thread with objcExportSuspendFunctionLaunchThreadRestriction=none. The screens' verification is T-374.
